headline: 40-run loss: Bangladesh bow out of Women's Asia Cup after India defeat
summary: A disappointing performance in all three departments sees the Bangladesh women's team exit the regional competition in the semifinals.
details: Bangladesh lost to India by 40 runs in the first semifinal of the Women's Asia Cup T20 in Dubai, ending their campaign in the regional tournament.
India posted a competitive 149 for six after batting first. Shafali Verma top-scored with 64 off 40 balls, while Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh provided late momentum.
Bangladesh kept India in check until the 15th over, but a late surge of 53 runs in the final five overs shifted the game. Sultana Khatun claimed 2-30 for Bangladesh.
caption:
A disappointing exit for the Tigresses. Bangladesh lose to India by 40 runs in the Women's Asia Cup semifinal.

Bangladesh lost to India by 40 runs in the first semifinal of the Women's Asia Cup T20 in Dubai, ending their campaign in the regional tournament.

India posted a competitive 149 for six after batting first. Shafali Verma top-scored with 64 off 40 balls, while Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh provided late momentum.

Bangladesh kept India in check until the 15th over, but a late surge of 53 runs in the final five overs shifted the game. Sultana Khatun claimed 2-30 for Bangladesh.

headline: Mymensingh man killed in Ukrainian drone strike in Russia
summary: A 25-year-old Bangladeshi man, promised a high-paying job as an electrician, was allegedly trafficked into the Russian military and killed during the conflict.
details: Mamun Mia, 25, from Mymensingh's Nandail upazila, was reportedly killed in a Ukrainian drone strike in Russia approximately two weeks ago.
His family and a fellow traveler, Rajon Hossain, allege that Mamun and around 30 other Bangladeshis were promised high-paying jobs as electricians via a recruiting agency.
The family claims that shortly after arriving in Russia on May 8, they were handed over to the Russian military, given weapons, and forced to take part in the the Russia-Ukraine war.
Rajon Hossain, who escaped and returned to Bangladesh on August 23, reported that Mamun's death was confirmed by a Russian-speaking commander who served as an interpreter.
Mamun was the sole earning member of his family, leaving behind a wife and two young children. His family had borrowed heavily to pay the recruiting agency Tk 8.5 lakh.
The family is demanding exemplary punishment for the trafficking ring and the recruiting agency involved, as well as government assistance to bring his body back.
Local police in Nandail have stated they are looking into the matter after learning about the incident through social media.
There has been no immediate independent confirmation of the death from the police or the Bangladesh embassy in Russia.
caption:
Promised a high-paying job as an electrician, a 25-year-old Bangladeshi man was allegedly trafficked into the Russian army and killed in a drone strike.

Mamun Mia, 25, from Mymensingh's Nandail upazila, was reportedly killed in a Ukrainian drone strike in Russia approximately two weeks ago.

His family and a fellow traveler, Rajon Hossain, allege that Mamun and around 30 other Bangladeshis were promised high-paying jobs as electricians via a recruiting agency.

The family claims that shortly after arriving in Russia on May 8, they were handed over to the Russian military, given weapons, and forced to take part in the the Russia-Ukraine war.

Rajon Hossain, who escaped and returned to Bangladesh on August 23, reported that Mamun's death was confirmed by a Russian-speaking commander who served as an interpreter.

Mamun was the sole earning member of his family, leaving behind a wife and two young children. His family had borrowed heavily to pay the recruiting agency Tk 8.5 lakh.

The family is demanding exemplary punishment for the trafficking ring and the recruiting agency involved, as well as government assistance to bring his body back.

Local police in Nandail have stated they are looking into the matter after learning about the incident through social media.

There has been no immediate independent confirmation of the death from the police or the Bangladesh embassy in Russia.
